claims.text: In CrFeCoNiX alloys, oxide stability above 900 °C is governed by the crystallographic and thermal-expansion compatibility between the oxide scale and substrate.
Changing X among Si, Mn, and Al tailors oxide/substrate crystallographic and thermal-expansion compatibility.
Si or Al promotes formation of dense, low-mismatch silica-, alumina-, or spinel-like oxide phases.
Dense, low-mismatch oxides enabled by Si or Al grow slowly and remain adherent.
Mn produces oxides with greater mismatch and lower adhesion than Si- or Al-containing alloys.
The greater mismatch and lower adhesion attributed to Mn cause oxide cracking or spallation.
The proposed initial material is a CrFeCoNiX alloy in a single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution state.
The intervention is exposure above 900 °C to an oxidative or corrosive atmosphere.
The atmosphere will have defined oxygen or corrosive-species partial pressures.
A close oxide/substrate thermal-expansion match minimizes interfacial stresses during thermal cycling.
Lower interfacial stress reduces the driving force for oxide cracking and spallation.
A larger thermal-expansion mismatch causes stress accumulation and mechanical failure of the oxide.
Si- or Al-containing alloys will retain a slow-growing, adherent oxide during prolonged exposure above 900 °C.
Mn-containing alloys will exhibit more cracking or spallation because of greater thermal-expansion mismatch and lower interfacial coherence.
CrFeCoNi without X is presumed to form a less protective oxide than favorable CrFeCoNiX compositions under the same conditions.
The hypothesis is limited to static high-temperature oxidative or corrosive conditions in which thermal cycling or rapid transient heating does not dominate oxidation kinetics.
Oxide thickness, growth rate, adhesion, phase constitution, residual stress, cracking, and spallation can be compared among Si-, Mn-, Al-containing alloys and a CrFeCoNi control.
The hypothesis is falsified if Si- or Al-containing alloys have cracking, spallation, or rapid growth statistically indistinguishable from the control or Mn-containing alloy.

contradictions.description: The stated boundary excludes conditions in which thermal cycling dominates oxidation kinetics, but the proposed experiment explicitly includes thermal cycles without specifying that cycling remains non-dominant.
